dm: May all the women in the world Become men. May those of lowly status attain high positions, And may their pride be utterly subdued.
gm: However many women there are in the world, May they become men. May the lowly obtain high status, And may their pride be subdued.

dm: By this merit of mine, May all sentient beings without exception, Having abandoned all misdeeds, Always engage in virtue.
gm: By this merit of mine, May all sentient beings without exception Abandon all harmful deeds And always perform virtuous ones.

dm: May they never be separated from the mind of enlightenment, May they be devoted to the conduct of awakening, May they be cared for by the Buddhas, And may they abandon the activities of Māra.
gm: Never separating from the awakening mind, And dedicating themselves to the bodhisattva conduct, May they be fully embraced by the buddhas, And abandon the actions of Māra.

dm: May all those sentient beings Have lives of immeasurable length; May they always live in happiness, And may even the sound of death never be heard.
gm: May all those sentient beings Have immeasurably long lives. May they always live happily, And may even the word "death" not be heard.

dm: May all directions be filled with groves of wish-fulfilling trees, Resounding with the sweet Dharma proclaimed By the Buddhas and the sons of the Buddhas, And may they be filled with these.
gm: With gardens of wish-fulfilling trees, Buddhas, and the children of buddhas Proclaiming the sweet sound of the Dharma, May all directions be filled.

dm: May the ground everywhere Be free from pebbles and the like, And remain naturally smooth, As level as the palm of a hand and of the nature of lapis lazuli.
gm: Everywhere, may the ground Be free of gravel and the like, As even as the palm of a hand, and of lapis lazuli, May its nature remain soft.

dm: In all the various circles of retinues, May many Bodhisattvas Dwell, having adorned the surface of the earth With their own excellence.
gm: In all the circles of retinues that exist, May many bodhisattvas Adorn the surface of the earth with their excellence, And remain dwelling there.

dm: May all embodied beings continuously hear The sound of the Dharma from birds, From trees, from all rays of light, And even from the sky itself.
gm: By all embodied beings, from birds, Trees, and all rays of light, And even from space, may the sound of the Dharma Be heard unceasingly.

dm: May they always meet with the Buddhas And the sons of the Buddhas. With infinite clouds of offerings, May they worship the teachers of the world.
gm: May they always encounter buddhas And the children of buddhas. With boundless clouds of offerings, May they make offerings to the gurus of the world.

dm: May the gods also send rain at the proper time, And may the harvests be bountiful. May kings act in accordance with the Dharma, And may the world also flourish.
gm: May the gods send rain on time, And may the harvests be perfect. May kings act in accordance with the Dharma, And may the world also prosper.

dm: May medicines be potent, And may the recitation of secret mantras be successful. May ḍākinīs, rākṣasas, and the like Be endowed with a mind of compassion.
gm: May medicines be endowed with potency, And may the recitation of secret mantras be accomplished. May ḍākinīs, rākṣasas, and the like Be endowed with minds of compassion.

dm: May no sentient being ever suffer, May they not be afraid or held in contempt, And may no one ever be unhappy.
gm: May no sentient being ever suffer, Or be afraid, or be belittled, And may none ever be unhappy.

dm: May temples be well-established, Adorned with study and recitation. May the Saṅgha always be in harmony, And may the purposes of the Saṅgha be accomplished.
gm: May monasteries, with reading and Recitation, remain well adorned. May the Saṅgha always be in harmony, And may the goals of the Saṅgha be accomplished.

dm: May those monks who desire to train Also obtain the state of solitude. Having abandoned all distractions, May they meditate with a workable mind.
gm: May monks who desire to train Attain solitary places. Having abandoned all distractions, May they meditate with pliable minds.

dm: May the nuns be endowed with requisites, And may they abandon quarreling and harm. Likewise, may all those who have gone forth Never let their ethical discipline decline.
gm: May nuns be endowed with provisions, And may they abandon quarrels and harm. Likewise, may all who are ordained Remain with unblemished discipline.

dm: Having become disillusioned by lapses in discipline, May they always exhaust their misdeeds. Having attained a higher rebirth, May their spiritual conduct not decline even there.
gm: May those with broken discipline feel remorse, And may they always exhaust their negative deeds. Having also attained higher realms, May their vows remain uncompromised even there.

dm: May the wise be honored, And may they also receive alms. May their mental continuums be completely purified, And may they be renowned in all directions.
gm: May the learned be honored And also receive alms. May their mindstreams be completely pure, And may they be renowned in all directions.

dm: May they not experience the suffering of the lower realms, And even without undergoing hardships, With bodies superior even to the gods, May they swiftly achieve Buddhahood.
gm: Without experiencing the sufferings of the lower realms, And without engaging in hardships, With bodies superior to those of the gods, May they swiftly attain buddhahood.

dm: May all sentient beings repeatedly Make offerings to all the Buddhas, And through the inconceivable bliss of the Buddhas, May they always be endowed with happiness.
gm: May all sentient beings repeatedly Make offerings to all the buddhas. With the inconceivable bliss of the buddhas, May they always be endowed with happiness.

dm: May the Bodhisattvas Fulfill their intentions to benefit wandering beings. Whatever the Protectors have intended, May that be attained by all sentient beings.
gm: May the bodhisattvas Accomplish their intentions for the welfare of beings. Whatever the protectors intend, May that be accomplished for sentient beings.

dm: Likewise, may the Pratyekabuddhas And the Śrāvakas also be happy.
gm: Likewise, may the pratyekabuddhas And the śrāvakas also be happy.

dm: Through the kindness of Mañjuśrī, Until I attain the Ground of Supreme Joy, May I always remember my past lives, And may I obtain the state of a renunciate.
gm: And through the kindness of Mañjuśrī, Until I attain the ground of Perfect Joy, May I always remember my past lives And attain ordination.

dm: May I be sustained and live, Even on a diet of the simplest food. In all my lives, may I obtain Perfect circumstances for living in solitude.
gm: May I, even with simple food, Live endowed with vitality. In all my lifetimes, May I attain the perfection of solitary places.

dm: Whenever I wish to see him, Or even wish to ask the slightest question, May I behold the Protector Mañjuśrī himself Without any hindrance.
gm: Whenever I wish to look, Or even wish to ask a slight question, May I behold the protector Mañjuśrī himself, Without any hindrance.

dm: For the sake of accomplishing the welfare of all sentient beings, Reaching to the very limits of space in the ten directions, Just as Mañjuśrī acts, May my conduct also be like that.
gm: As far as the limits of space in the ten directions, In order to accomplish the aims of all sentient beings, Just as Mañjuśrī acts, May my conduct also be like that.

dm: For as long as space remains, And for as long as sentient beings remain, Until then, may I too remain, To dispel the sufferings of the world.
gm: As long as space abides, And as long as beings remain, So long may I also remain, To dispel the suffering of beings.

dm: Whatever sufferings sentient beings have, May they all ripen upon me. Through the assembly of Bodhisattvas, May all beings enjoy happiness.
gm: Whatever suffering there is for beings, May it all ripen upon me. Through the sangha of bodhisattvas, May beings experience happiness.

dm: May the teaching—the sole medicine for the suffering of beings And the source of all happiness— Endure for a long time, Together with support and honor.
gm: The sole medicine for the suffering of beings, The source of all happiness, May the teaching, along with gain and honor, Remain for a long time.

dm: I prostrate to Mañjughoṣa, Through whose kindness a virtuous mind arises. I also prostrate to my spiritual friend, Through whose kindness I have flourished.
gm: Through whose kindness a virtuous mind arises, I prostrate to Mañjuśrī. Through whose kindness I have grown, I also prostrate to the spiritual friend.

dm: This concludes the tenth chapter, entitled "Dedication," from the *Entering the Way of the Bodhisattva*.
gm: The tenth chapter, called Dedication, from Entering the Way of the Bodhisattva.

dm: Colophon
gm: Author's Colophon

dm: The *Entering the Way of the Bodhisattva*, composed by the master Śāntideva, is hereby completed.
gm: Entering the Way of the Bodhisattva, composed by the master Śāntideva, is complete.

dm: Colophon
gm: Translator's Colophon

dm: This was translated, edited, and finalized from a Kashmiri manuscript by the Indian scholar Sarvajñādeva and the chief editor-translator Bandé Paltseg.
gm: Revised and finalized by the Indian preceptor Sarvajñādeva and the chief editor-translator, the monk Paltsek, based on a Kashmiri manuscript;

dm: Later, the Indian scholar Dharmaśrībhadra and the chief editors and translators, the monks Rinchen Zangpo and Śākya Lodrö, revised, translated, and finalized it in accordance with a Central Indian manuscript and commentary.
gm: Later, it was corrected, translated, and finalized by the Indian preceptor Dharmaśrībhadra and the chief editor-translators, the monk Rinchen Zangpo and Śākya Lodrö, in accordance with manuscripts and commentaries from the central region.

dm: Furthermore, at a later time, the Indian scholar Sumatikīrti and the chief editor and translator, the monk Loden Sherab, accurately revised, translated, and thoroughly finalized it.
gm: Still later, it was correctly revised, translated, and excellently finalized by the Indian preceptor Sumatikīrti and the chief editor-translator, the fully ordained monk Loden Sherab.
